_comment: Tier-2 for febio::active_contraction#3. A near-step activation (full amplitude in the first fiftieth of the run) and a linear ramp over the whole run, both under <analysis>STATIC</analysis>: both complete every step with exit 0, neither prints '------- failed to converge at time', and their final node positions agree to well within five decimal places. This is the executed form of the entry's own falsification of an older claim that a step change in T0 makes the first step fail and that SMOOTH interpolation is required. Executed 2026-08-06 on FEBio 4.12.0.86045466d (source build, USE_MKL=OFF). MUTATION CONTROL (2026-08-07): MUTATION APPLIED AND IT DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE. T2_MUTATE=1 neutralises the L.swap edits so both runs use the SAME deck; the fixture still PASSES, with max_abs_difference_in_final_position=0.000e+00 and agree_to_five_decimals=1 (measured 2026-08-07). That is structural rather than a defect in the mutation: this fixture asserts an EQUALITY -- that two activation ramps give the same converged answer -- and an equality is satisfied a fortiori when the two decks are identical. There is no pathology here to remove; removing the edits removes the comparison. What the fixture is missing is a POSITIVE CONTROL: a third deck this same measurement DOES separate, say the same STATIC run at a different T0, proving that max_abs_difference_in_final_position can be large and that agree_to_five_decimals is therefore informative. Without it, diff < 1e-5 cannot tell 'the ramp shape does not matter' from 'the two runs were the same run'. The hook is left in source.py so the negative result is re-runnable: `cd <fixture dir> && T2_MUTATE=1 ~/Schreibtisch/open-fem-agent/.venv/bin/python source.py`.
